main_text.p: pologia Origenis a, a Dissert. de Ignat. p. 85. Ab his qui Origenis libros legunt, istud penitus putant exclusum esse mandatum, quo probabiles jubentur effici trapezitæ, scientes, quod bonum est retinere, ab omni autem specie mali se abstinere. Dubitari non potest, quin Eusebius, æque ac Clemens, & Basilius ad Paulum respiciat, cujus totam illam in priore ad Thessalonicenses φῆσιν recitat. b T.3.op. Bas. p. 36.col.2. aut.med. Fronto quidem Ducæus b, nobilis Iesuita, ea de re non dubitavit, qui ad illum Basilii locum habet. Quæ sequuntur, ut bonus trapezita &c. alludunt ad illud Apostoli 1. Thessal. 5. 21. πάντα δοκιμάζοντες, &c.
Eodemque refert illa Gregorii Nazianzeni c, sane appositissimè; c Iamb. 18.
main_text.l: Ἀγχυρογνώμων, εἴ τι μὴ καλὸν δέχῃ·
Ἀπεληλέγξ δ' ἂν μή σε ποιεῖ βελτίω.

main_text.p: Non dubitavit eruditissimus, atq; optimus Syburgius noster, qui in notis ad locum Clementis nuper descriptum, Allusio (inquit d) est ad dictum Pauli 1. Thess. 5. Ex his nemo non videt, nihil esse necesse ad διαταγέας confugere, vel concedere eos isto-d p. 832. A.

page.notes: The Greek lines are printed in small type; the second Greek line of the verse and the word "διαταγέας" are uncertain. "Syburgius" appears as printed; the initial letters of the first line are partly damaged. The Greek word in the verse at "Ἀγχυρογνώμων" is doubtful. Marginal notes a, b, c, d are set beside their lines in the right margin.
